{{Short description|Chinese mathematician and probability theorist}}
<!-- AfC submission header: keep this first line if submitting through Articles for Creation (Draft:Jian Ding). If publishing directly to mainspace instead, delete this line. -->

'''Jian Ding''' ({{zh|s=丁剑}}) is a Chinese mathematician and probability theorist. He is a chair professor at the School of Mathematical Sciences of [[Peking University]], where he also serves as vice dean.<ref name="ycwb">{{cite news |title=北大6名学者喜获千万级研究资助 |url=https://edu.ycwb.com/2025-11/26/content_53816113.htm |work=[[Yangcheng Evening News]] |date=26 November 2025 |language=zh |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref> In 2023 he was awarded the [[Loève Prize]].<ref name="ims">{{cite web |title=Jian Ding wins 2023 Loève Prize |url=https://imstat.org/2023/11/15/jian-ding-wins-2023-loeve-prize/ |publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |date=15 November 2023 |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="berkeley">{{cite web |title=Jian Ding Ph.D. 2011, Wins Loève Prize |url=https://statistics.berkeley.edu/about/news/jian-ding-phd-2011-wins-loeve-prize |publisher=Department of Statistics, University of California, Berkeley |date=23 October 2023 |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Ding entered Peking University in 2002 and received his bachelor's degree in mathematics in 2006.<ref name="nus">{{cite web |title=Lecture Series in Statistics – Prof. Jian Ding |url=https://www.stat.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2025/01/Lecture-Series-in-Statistics-Prof.-Jian-Ding.pdf |publisher=Department of Statistics and Data Science, National University of Singapore |date=January 2025 |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref> He earned his PhD in statistics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2011, under the supervision of [[Yuval Peres]].<ref name="berkeley"/><ref name="mgp">{{cite web |title=Jian Ding |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=153950 |publisher=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]] |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref>

After postdoctoral positions at the [[University of Washington]] and as a Szegö Assistant Professor at [[Stanford University]], Ding joined the faculty of the [[University of Chicago]], where he became an associate professor in the Department of Statistics. He then moved to the [[University of Pennsylvania]], where he was the Gilbert Helman Professor in the [[Wharton School]]. In January 2022 he returned to Peking University as a chair professor.<ref name="berkeley"/><ref name="nus"/>

== Research ==
Ding's research is in probability theory, in particular its interactions with [[statistical physics]] and [[theoretical computer science]]. His work has covered random walks, Gaussian processes, random constraint satisfaction problems, random planar geometry, spin models, and Anderson localization.<ref name="ims"/><ref name="ams">{{cite journal |title=Ding Wins Loeve Prize |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |date=February 2024 |volume=71 |issue=2 |pages=279–280 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/202402/rnoti-p279.pdf}}</ref> With Allan Sly and Nike Sun, he proved the satisfiability threshold conjecture for random [[k-SAT]] for large k.<ref name="davidson">{{cite journal |title=Applied Probability Trust Prizes 2017 |journal=Journal of Applied Probability |year=2017 |volume=54 |issue=2 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/78CA2FAD124068DBE3AED17042725A70/S0021900217000031a.pdf |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]}}</ref><ref name="ams2017">{{cite journal |title=2017 Rollo Davidson Prize Awarded |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=August 2017 |volume=64 |issue=7 |page=768}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship]] (2015)<ref name="nus"/>
* NSF CAREER Award (2015)<ref name="ims"/>
* [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] (2017, shared with Nike Sun)<ref name="davidson"/><ref name="ams2017"/>
* Invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (2022, joint lecture with Julien Dubédat and Ewain Gwynne)<ref name="icm">{{cite book |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians 2022 |chapter=Jian Ding, Julien Dubédat, Ewain Gwynne, Introduction to the Liouville quantum gravity metric |publisher=EMS Press |volume=5 |page=4212 |url=https://content.ems.press/assets/public/full-texts/books/277/online-pdf/978-3-98547-563-6-volume-5.pdf}}</ref>
* Gold Medal of Mathematics of the International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians (2022)<ref name="iccm">{{cite web |title=Past Awards – ICCM Medal of Mathematics |url=https://iccm.simis.cn/iccm2025/site/awards/past-awards/ |publisher=[[International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians]] |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref>
* [[Loève Prize]] (2023)<ref name="ims"/><ref name="ams"/>
* IMS Medallion Lecture (2023)<ref name="medallion">{{cite web |title=Preview of Medallion Lecture: Jian Ding |url=https://imstat.org/2023/02/15/preview-of-medallion-lecture-jian-ding/ |publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |date=15 February 2023 |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref>
* Plenary speaker at the International Congress on Mathematical Physics (2024)<ref name="nus"/>
* Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (2025)<ref name="imsfellow">{{cite web |title=Congratulations to the 2025 Class of IMS Fellows! |url=https://imstat.org/2025/05/05/congratulations-to-the-2025-class-of-ims-fellows/ |publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |date=5 May 2025 |access-date=25 August 2026}}</ref>
